concepts.def: Sacrament of unity between man and woman until death (Catholic); some Anglicans bless same-sex unions; vows include faithfulness.
Contract requiring offer, acceptance, witnesses, mahr (dowry); permits up to four wives with equal treatment; polygamy rare today.
Christianity: discouraged but accepted (Anglican remarriage allowed); Islam: triple talaq (Sunni); Catholicism only annulment.
Catholic ban on artificial methods (Humanae Vitae 1968); Protestants generally accept; Islam permits with mutual consent.
Diverse views: progressive Christians/Jews celebrate; Catholic, Orthodox, most Muslim/Hindu/Sikh traditions oppose; debate over Bible passages.
Religions emphasise parental love and child obligations; Honour Father and Mother (Exodus 20); Confucian filial piety.

walkthroughs.body_html:
An Introduction to Philosophy of Religion — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

An Introduction to Philosophy of Religion brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with An Introduction to Philosophy of Religion.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
